title: The Story of Yusuf and the Brothers Who Wronged Him
script: Narrator: [warmly] Long ago, a boy named Yusuf had a dream about eleven stars and the sun bowing down to him.
Narrator: [thoughtful] His father, Prophet Yaqub, understood the dream meant something great, and told Yusuf to keep it quiet.
Narrator: [sadly] Yusuf's own brothers grew jealous of him, because their father loved him deeply and openly.
Narrator: [with sorrow] One day, driven by jealousy, the brothers threw Yusuf into a deep well and left him there alone.
Narrator: [reflective] A passing caravan found him and, sadly, sold him into slavery far away, in the land of Egypt.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Yusuf faced many hardships there, even being falsely accused and thrown into prison for years he did not deserve.
Narrator: [warmly] But Allah gave Yusuf the ability to interpret dreams, and this gift eventually reached the king himself.
Narrator: [with hope] Yusuf interpreted a dream about a coming famine, and his wise advice saved all of Egypt from starvation.
Narrator: [amazed] He rose from prisoner to a powerful position, trusted completely by the king to manage the entire land.
Narrator: [reflective] Years later, during that same famine, his brothers traveled to Egypt seeking food, not knowing who stood before them.
Narrator: [softly] Yusuf recognized them immediately, though they did not recognize him after so many years apart.
Narrator: [with feeling] Finally, Yusuf revealed himself, and his brothers froze in fear, remembering exactly what they had done to him.
Narrator: [gently] But Yusuf did not punish them. He said simply, no blame upon you today. Allah will forgive you.
Narrator: [warmly] That forgiveness, after everything he suffered, remains one of the most moving moments in his entire story.
Narrator: [with a small smile] Yusuf's patience through hardship, and his mercy afterward, still teaches us both endurance and forgiveness today.
